title: Grade Manager Core With JSON Persistence

visible.label: Tracks student scores, overwrites duplicates, and computes averages
visible.inputDisplay: add S1 quiz=80 then overwrite quiz=90 + lab=100 -> avg 95.0
visible.script:
gb = GradeBook()
gb.add_score("S1", "quiz", 80)
gb.add_score("S1", "quiz", 90)
gb.add_score("S1", "lab", 100)
assert abs(gb.student_average("S1") - 95.0) < 1e-6

visible.label: Persists and restores full state via JSON file
visible.expectedDisplay: Restored GradeBook matches averages and top_students
visible.script:
gb = GradeBook()
gb.add_score("S2", "exam", 88.5)
gb.add_score("S1", "exam", 95.0)
path = "/tmp/p092_vis.json"
gb.save_json(path)
restored = GradeBook.load_json(path)
assert abs(restored.student_average("S2") - 88.5) < 1e-6
assert restored.top_students(2) == [("S1", 95.0), ("S2", 88.5)]

hidden.label: Out-of-range score rejects with ValueError
Boundary scores 0 and 100 are accepted cleanly
hidden.script:
gb = GradeBook()
gb.add_score("S1", "a", 0)
gb.add_score("S1", "b", 100)
assert abs(gb.student_average("S1") - 50.0) < 1e-6

hidden.label: Unknown student raises KeyError
top_students breaks equal averages alphabetically ascending
hidden.script:
gb = GradeBook()
gb.add_score("B", "e", 90)
gb.add_score("A", "e", 90)
gb.add_score("C", "e", 80)
assert gb.top_students(2) == [("A", 90.0), ("B", 90.0)]

hidden.label: top_students(0) and load_json missing file behavior
hidden.script:
gb = GradeBook()
gb.add_score("A", "e", 90)
assert gb.top_students(0) == []
try:
    GradeBook.load_json("/tmp/definitely_missing_p092.json")
    assert False
except FileNotFoundError:
    pass

hints: Store scores in nested dicts `{student_id: {assessment: float(score)}}` so repeated `add_score` calls naturally overwrite the same assessment.
For `top_students(k)`, sort `(student_id, avg)` with key `lambda item: (-item[1], item[0])`.
Serialize nested dicts cleanly with `json.dump(..., fp, indent=2)` and reload via a `@classmethod` reconstructing a new `GradeBook`.
